summary: Configured node1 with RHEL 10’s Redis-compatible Valkey 8 service, durable AOF and RDB storage, and a dedicated authenticated inventory identity. The generated credential is stored at /etc/redis-inventory.env as root:root mode 0600. Service and data successfully recovered after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled the native Valkey service.
Configured AOF persistence with every-second fsync and scheduled RDB snapshots under /var/lib/valkey.
Generated the inventory credential on node1 and stored only its hash in the Valkey ACL file.
Verified authenticated inventory reads and writes through node1’s managed IP.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified a changed boot identity, service recovery, authentication, and persisted data.

evidence.summary: Shows persistent configuration, enabled/active service, managed-IP listener, runtime appendonly=yes, successful snapshot, and physical AOF/RDB files.
Authenticated PING returns PONG, ACL identity is inventory, reads/writes succeed, and unauthenticated access returns NOAUTH before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Generated credential stored with root-only access
evidence.summary: The credential was generated on node1; /etc/redis-inventory.env is root:root mode 0600, and an explicit access test as the valkey account was denied.

Healthy baseline used boot ID e625b9a5-4242-499a-88da-9a76ecf86fe1; reboot was acknowledged; node returned with boot ID 6969aed0-ab82-4e8e-8434-d5980fefd1f2; enabled service, inventory authentication, persistence health, listeners, and the pre-reboot value all recovered.
